title: Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh assassinated in Tehran
body:
Ismail Haniyeh, the head of Hamas's political bureau, was killed at around 2:00 a.m. Iran Standard Time on 31 July 2024 at a guesthouse in Tehran, Iran. He had attended the inauguration of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian the previous day. His aide and bodyguard, Wassim Abu Shaaban, was also killed. The New York Times described the site as an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-run guesthouse in the Neshat compound, near Sa'dabad.

Accounts of the method differed. The IRGC said Haniyeh was killed by a short-range projectile carrying about 7 kilograms of explosives, fired from outside the building. The New York Times reported that a bomb had been smuggled into the guesthouse months earlier and was detonated remotely. Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz confirmed Israel's responsibility in December 2024. Hours earlier, Israel had announced the killing of Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr in Beirut.

Hamas mourned Haniyeh and called the killing a treacherous Zionist raid, saying it would not pass in vain. Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei vowed revenge, and on 1 October 2024 Iran launched about 200 ballistic missiles at Israel, citing Haniyeh's killing among its reasons.
